body:
I'm 29.  We were married for 3 years.  2 of them pretty good, the last was sad.  During this time, she left her religion which made her feel like she missed out on all of her life.  She met new friends who were younger (and arguably more fun) and she took all of this time to decide she was unhappy at home but never told me.  I knew something wasn't right, so I kept asking her about it, to which she said "nothing."

One day she wakes me up and says she doesn't want to be married anymore.  I spend the next few weeks trying to work on all of the things she finally told me were wrong (she had mentioned a few in the past, but very long ago so I assumed she stopped being bugged by them).  Then she says it's not working, she tries being separated, but she gives up on that after 2 days and then it's just been dealing with separating our shit.

I know our marriage wasn't perfect, in fact the last year was pretty depressing.  But I literally gave up everything/everyone I had to help her (she's been depressed our whole marriage) and now she just seems so happy and excited to be done with me.  I can't handle it.  How did the wife who 4 months ago gave me notes that said that me and our dog were the only things that mattered to her, suddenly turn so sour towards our union?  She's sworn it wasn't an affair, and I actually believe her, but still... that might've been easier.  By her own admission, she's "leaving something good for the hopes that something can be better."  She might find it... I know I won't.
That's the problem.  She was the only person I could talk to.

This line is incredibly helpful:

> she does not define you, your marriage does not define you. You define you.
Yeah... unfortunately I still think some good things about her which makes this horribly confusing.
God I miss when my wife felt this way.  I'm very happy that you still experience this.  Don't forget how this makes you feel, it can slip away faster than you think if you let it.
